newsitem.title: LATVIA: Parity row could stop Aeroflot flights to Riga.
newsitem.headline: Parity row could stop Aeroflot flights to Riga.

text.p: The Latvian transport ministry said on Tuesday that it might suspend flights by Russia's Aeroflot and Transaero airlines to the Latvian capital from Thursday if a parity row is not resolved.
The Latvian transport ministry says its Russian counterpart is not recognising the principle of parity outlined in international aviation conventions.
Two Russian air-carriers, Aeroflot and Transaero, have scheduled flights to Riga. Only one Latvian air-carrier, Riair, has regular flights to Russia.
Latvia says that Air Baltic should also be allowed to fly routes to Russia and that the number of flights should be the same for both sides.

"If the flight parity issue remains unresolved, the Latvian side will not approve the winter flight schedule for Russian aviation companies," Arnis Muiznieks, head of the aviation department in the Latvian transport ministry, told Reuters.
"The first Russian flights to be cancelled are scheduled for Thursday," he said, adding that a deal between the two sides had been ready for two years but Russia had refused to sign it.
He added that Transaero might be excluded from the ban as it had a code-sharing agreement with Riair.
Aeroflot has four scheduled flights per week to Riga.
